ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding screening of all UBOs, directors, officers and authorized signatories against the HM Treasury Consolidated List (UK sanctions), United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) enforcement and warning lists. PEP status must be determined on a risk-sensitive basis with enhanced due diligence required for any politically exposed person. Ongoing transaction monitoring and screening refresh at minimum every 90 days; the headhunting retainer payment rails (Retainer_Wire and Wise_B2B) must be independently vetted for sanctioned counterparties prior to each disbursement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry (Registrar of Companies) — name search and reservation routed through the Gibraltar e-Government portal (egov.gi / Companies Registry online search facility)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company and branch names must be in Latin script using English; non-Latin scripts are not accepted. The name of a limited company must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. For an overseas company (foreign branch), the registered name must match the Bermuda Exempted Company's constitutional name and may be registered under that name or an alternate permitted business name in English. Names cannot contain misleading references to activities not authorized, and any distinctive suffix must not create confusion with an existing registered corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 30 days. A single renewal for an additional 30 days may be requested before expiry, subject to availability and payment of the applicable renewal fee. If the Registrar rejects the proposed name, the applicant must submit a fresh application with a modified name. A rejected applicant may file a formal written appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 21 calendar days of the rejection notice, stating the grounds of objection and providing evidence of distinctiveness. The Registrar must issue a decision within 28 calendar days of receipt. An adverse decision may be further challenged by way of judicial review proceedings before the Supreme Court of Gibraltar. All appeal and court procedures require a registered Gibraltar address for service.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permitted only as the registered-office element of the Gibraltar overseas company registration, provided a substantive physical presence in Gibraltar (dedicated office space or serviced office with staff) is established for the executive search and headhunting operations. Pure virtual-only arrangements without a physical operational footprint will fail the Gibraltar Economic Substance assessment for the active business income and may invalidate the tax-exempt status of the Bermuda Exempted Company structure if managed and controlled from Gibraltar.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% (moderate-low risk of unannounced physical inspection by the Gibraltar Companies Registry or GFSC, increasing to 35% if the entity derives all income from Gibraltar invoicing or if the Economic Substance return flags operational presence anomalies; executive search and headhunting ISIC 7830 is treated as a standard low-risk activity but remains subject to regular compliance monitoring)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, ss. 4-7 (incorporation), s. 5 (share capital), s. 6 (statement of compliance), s. 30 (memorandum and articles), s. 75 (registered office), s. 180 (directors and secretary).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Her Majesty's Government of Gibraltar — Companies House Gibraltar e-Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form CO-1 (Application for Incorporation) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association, submitted to the Registrar of Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an exempted company incorporated in Gibraltar. Subscriber shares must be issued with a stated nominal value, typically GBP 1.00 per share. No escrow account is required; a statutory declaration of compliance under s. 6 Companies Act 2014 is filed by the registered agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], a Gibraltar-incorporated exempted company. HELD at the registered office on [date]. 1. RESOLVED that the subscriber share allotment be ratified and the register of members be opened in accordance with the Memorandum and Articles of Association. 2. RESOLVED that the registered office at [street address], Gibraltar, be adopted as the company's statutory registered office. 3. RESOLVED that [Director Name] be appointed as sole director, [Secretary Name] as company secretary, and [Compliance Officer Name] as designated compliance officer under the AML framework. 4. RESOLVED that the directors be authorised to procure all registry filings, engage the registered agent, and open corporate bank accounts with the approved EMI and licensed bank. ADOPTED unanimously on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Her Majesty's Government of Gibraltar — e-Registry online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed company name through the approved registered agent using the e-Registry name search facility. The Registry issues an electronic name reservation certificate once the name passes the availability and sensitivity screening. The reservation is valid for 60 days pending incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Company type and registered agent details
Authorisation letter from the intended directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the registered agent may file a written representation to the Registrar within 14 days and simultaneously submit two alternative names for expedited re-screening. Refusal grounds are stated by the Registry and can be cured by amending the name to remove prohibited terms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarisation of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved corporate service provider and Gibraltar Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage the licensed registered agent to draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association tailored to the exempted company status, including the exclusion of Gibraltar tax residency and adoption of the permitted object clause. Execute the subscriber pages before a Notary Public, with apostille certification by the Gibraltar Attorney General's Chambers where required for overseas bank or client due diligence.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director and company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies incomplete identity evidence or inconsistent clauses, return with corrected documents and a supplemental statutory declaration within 5 business days. The registered agent may seek binding legal guidance from the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission if the constitutional clauses raise regulatory ambiguity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment of Registry Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House Gibraltar — Registrar of Companies, HM Government of Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent lodges Form CO-1 via the e-Registry portal, attaching the notarised Memorandum and Articles, consents, and registered office consent. The statutory filing fee is paid online by card or bank transfer. The Registrar performs a compliance review and issues a sealed Certificate of Incorporation upon satisfaction.
required_dossiers: Form CO-1 signed by subscribers and authorised agent
Consents of first directors and secretary
Registered office consent and utility proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for missing or defective schedules, the registered agent will receive a written requisition. Corrected documentation must be resubmitted within 21 days; the first re-filing incurs no additional state fee. Should the Registrar reject the application, a new Form CO-1 with the Registrar's objections cured can be filed within a further 14-day period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Adoption of Corporate Governance Framework
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors convened at the registered office through the corporate service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting in compliance with the Articles. Ratify the subscriber share allotment, adopt the registered office, appoint the directors, secretary and compliance officer, and approve the corporate governance manual, anti-money laundering policy and data protection policies as required for an executive headhunting agency. Record minutes in the statutory books and issue share certificates.
required_dossiers: First board meeting agenda and draft minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the meeting lacks quorum, the board may hold an adjourned meeting within 7 days under the Articles. If a director's conflict arises, the conflicted director must abstain and the remaining disinterested directors may proceed. Any defect in minutes may be cured by a supplemental unanimous written resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Enrolment and Operating Licence Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office; Employment Services Board, Department of Labour, HM Government of Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of incorporation, the company files its taxpayer registration with the Income Tax Office and obtains a corporate tax reference. Simultaneously, submit the operating licence application for private employment and executive search services under the Private Employment Agencies Act. The licence application requires the board minute confirming compliance with AML, client money safeguarding, and the data protection standards. The Employment Services Board conducts a fit-and-proper review before issuing the licence.
required_dossiers: First board minutes and certificate of incumbency
Fit-and-proper evidence of directors and compliance officer
AML policies and professional indemnity insurance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is queried, file a revised COR-1 with a correction notice within 15 days. If the Employment Services Board objects to the licence application, the company may submit written representations and additional supporting evidence within 21 days, with a right of appeal to the Minister for Labour under the Employment Agencies Regulations. Temporary authorisation may be granted pending the appeal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Employment Services Board, Department of Labour, HM Government of Gibraltar
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Private Employment Agency Licence (Executive Search and Headhunting) issued under the Private Employment Agencies Act 2010

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration — Low-Impact Commercial Office Use (No Full EIA Required)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Gibraltar Waste Management Regulations 2016 for disposal of hard-copy records; volatile organic compound emissions from cleaning and disinfection products below 50 mg/Nm³; wastewater discharge only to municipal sewers with a valid trade effluent consent where applicable; no hazardous waste streams expected. An annual environmental return is required only if staffing exceeds 20 FTE.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Valid Fire Safety Certificate issued by the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service under the Fire Safety Act 2020; structural load inspection certificate from the Building Control Authority confirming the office floor loading capacity; workplace occupation clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1998, including emergency evacuation plans, first-aid equipment, and DDA-compliant access.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar Income Tax Office, operating under the Commissioner of Income Tax; self-service portal at https://portal.tax.gi (Gibraltar Revenue Services (GRS) e-filing system).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign Bermuda Exempted Companies establishing economic substance in Gibraltar must: (1) apply for registration at Companies House Gibraltar under the Companies Act 2014, filing the constitutional documents and registered office address; (2) submit Form GIP-1 (Gibraltar Introduction of Profits) where applicable; (3) complete the Taxpayer Registration Application with GRS through a licensed Gibraltar tax representative or resident agent; (4) obtain a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN) from the Income Tax Office, typically issued within 10–15 working days; (5) register for employee payroll (PAYE) and social insurance (GSSP) with the Director of Employment if hiring Gibraltar-based staff; (6) maintain a registered office and resident company secretary; (7) file an annual return and obtain the Certificate of Good Standing. No prior approval from Bermuda authorities is required for a foreign-managed Exempted Company, but statutory books must remain available for inspection in Gibraltar.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (Bermuda domicile, as a non-resident owned Exempted Company) combined with Entity_Level_Taxation in Gibraltar. A Bermuda Exempted Company that is managed and controlled from or carries on a trade through a permanent establishment in Gibraltar becomes Gibraltar tax resident and is subject to the 12.5% corporate income tax on Gibraltar-source and remittance-basis profits. Territorial_Scope applies only to the Bermudian exempt status; Gibraltar follows the OECD 2014 substance-over-form framework and requires economic substance in the jurisdiction of management to avoid reclassification as a shell entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Gibraltar 'check-the-box' or US-style entity classification election exists. Statutory elections available: (a) election under Section 15(3) Income Tax Act 2010 for a company to be treated as tax resident in Gibraltar on the basis of incorporation (for UK–Gibraltar dual residency purposes); (b) application for exemption from quarantine under the Income Tax (Exempt Companies) (Amendment) Regulations, applicable only to pre-2011 exempt certificates; (c) the OECD Hybrid Mismatch Rules (Income Tax (Hybrid Mismatch) Regulations 2021) require an elective notification to GRS for avoiding or substantiating an asymmetric treatment between Bermuda's full exemption and Gibraltar's 12.5% rate; (d) Group relief election under Section 47A for loss surrender among Gibraltar-resident group members. Bermuda does not impose tax on the Exempted Company, so no Bermuda tax election is required; however, a Gibraltar–Bermuda permanent establishment relief election may be lodged to mitigate double taxation on profits attributed to the Gibraltar branch.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT, GST, or sales tax in Gibraltar. Gibraltar is a separate customs territory from the United Kingdom and the EU, operating a customs and excise duty regime under the Customs Duties Ordinance 1937 and the Goods (Importation and Exportation) Ordinance. A General Consumption Tax (GCT) has been proposed but not enacted.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable. No general consumption tax registration threshold exists. However, importers of goods into Gibraltar must register with the Customs Department for a Customs Declarant Code (CDN) and obtain an Economic Operator Registration and Identification (EORI) equivalent, required for any import customs declaration, regardless of turnover. Commercial service exports (executive search fees) do not trigger any indirect tax registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping mandate exists in Gibraltar for B2B services. Invoices must comply with Section 55 of the Income Tax Act 2010 substantiation requirements. Gibraltar customs clearance uses the electronic ASYCUDA World system for import/export declarations; duties on business samples and marketing collateral are payable at import unless covered by temporary importation provisions. There is no requirement to have invoices validated by the tax authority prior to issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — Gibraltar has no VAT system. Cross-border executive search and headhunting services supplied by a Gibraltar-resident Bermuda Exempted Company to non-Gibraltar clients are 'neither taxed nor zero-rated', falling wholly outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect taxation. Consequently, no input VAT credit or export refund mechanism exists. For direct tax purposes, the service is treated as exported and is exempt from Gibraltar corporate tax only to the extent the income is not attributable to a Gibraltar permanent establishment or management-and-control activities; if the contract, payment, and decision-making are located outside Gibraltar, the profits are outside Gibraltar's territorial charge. The client's country will normally apply a reverse-charge or self-assessment VAT mechanism on the imported executive search service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable for services; for substantiation of export treatment GRS requires: signed engagement agreement between the Gibraltar entity and the offshore client, stating the place of supply and absence of Gibraltar benefit
Itemised commercial invoices detailing the retained executive search scope, deliverables, and fee milestones
Evidence of offshore contract negotiation (e.g., outbound comms, meeting records, client-side project briefs)
Bank wire remittance confirmations from the foreign client (SWIFT MT103) matched to invoiced amounts
Foreign exchange conversion certificates to prove the remittance of invoice proceeds into the Gibraltar trading account
KYC documentation of the foreign client (entity registration, beneficial ownership structure) consistent with Gibraltar AML/CFT legislation
Annual Economic Substance Return (ESR) appendix confirming that core income-generating activities (headhunting) are not performed in Gibraltar unless properly attributed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Although no VAT clawback applies (no VAT system), GRS Direct Tax Audit and the Customs Department scrutinise export substantiation for transfer pricing and diversion of Gibraltar-source profits. Penalties under the Income Tax Act 2010: (a) understatement of profits due to non-remitted export income — up to 100% of additional tax plus interest at 4% above the applicable base rate; (b) late economic substance filings — automatic administrative penalty of GBP 1,000 and potential strike-off; (c) fraudulent misdeclaration of place-of-supply to avoid tax — criminal prosecution under Section 92(1) with fines up to GBP 50,000 and up to 7 years' imprisonment for directors; (d) retroactive reassessment period extends to 6 years for non-negligent errors and 20 years for deliberate concealment (Sections 98–99). Failure to repatriate export earnings within the 180-day deadline without a commercially justified reason triggers re-characterisation of the amount as a director's loan or deemed distribution, attracting dividend withholding at 0% but additional assessment under CFC rules. To avoid clawback, the company must retain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation under the OECD TP Guidelines, including a functional analysis proving that all high-value headhunting decisions (candidate sourcing, negotiations, fee setting) are executed outside Gibraltar.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Government of Gibraltar Currency Commission (official issuer of Gibraltar Pound GIP at 1:1 GBP parity); monetary policy conducted by the Bank of England; bank licensing and prudential supervision by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) under the Financial Services Act 2019
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar maintains full and unrestricted convertibility on both capital and current account transactions; the Gibraltar Pound is exchangeable at par with GBP and circulates interchangeably with sterling. No exchange control law, no surrender duty, and no prior authorisation from the GFSC or the Currency Commission is required for inbound equity capital, intercompany funding, retainer fee receipts, or outbound profit remittances. Profit remittance hurdles are purely documentary: the Bermuda Exempted Company must evidence economic substance in Bermuda or Gibraltar (Bermuda Economic Substance Declaration Form ES-1, Gibraltar ES Certificate of Compliance), maintain a CRS/FATCA registration with a valid GI TIN, and present audited or reviewed financial statements confirming distributable reserves; Gibraltar levies no dividend withholding tax and no capital gains tax on non-resident shareholders, subject to compliance with the Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar) and the UK-Gibraltar double taxation agreement provisions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Neither Gibraltar nor Bermuda imposes statutory export proceeds surrender timelines, mandatory conversion ratios, or repatriation quotas. Executive search and headhunting services exported from the Gibraltar entity may be invoiced and collected in GBP, EUR, USD, or any freely convertible currency and held in the corresponding bank account without conversion obligation. For AML/CFT purposes, each export receipt must be matched to an underlying commercial contract and invoice, with the original SWIFT MT103 or equivalent payment instruction retained in the customer due diligence file.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (multi-currency GBP/EUR/USD)
Operational Account and Trade Settlement Clearing Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco Santander Totta S.A. - Gibraltar Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Restricted but usable as a secondary treasury rail only. UK-authorised Electronic Money Institutions (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business) are not passportable into Gibraltar post-Brexit, and a Gibraltar branch of a UK EMI would require a separate GFSC e-money authorisation under the Financial Services Act 2019. Wise B2B is feasible for low-value operational retainers, candidate expense reimbursement, and contractor disbursements below GBP 25,000 per transaction, provided the EMI performs its own KYC and the Gibraltar entity maintains a recognised banking fallback with a Tier 1 licensed credit institution. Fully digital onboarding with Wise or Currencycloud is viable for ancillary flows but the capital escrow account and all client-retainer settlement accounts must be maintained with a GFSC-licensed bank to preserve creditor protection and audit trail integrity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person director appearance is mandatory in practice. The GFSC licensed banks and their MLROs require at least one natural-person director, final beneficial owner, or the appointed Gibraltar Authorised Representative to attend a face-to-face onboarding interview at the bank's premises or at the registered office of the licensed corporate services provider. Remote opening via video KYC is occasionally permitted for existing clients, but for a Bermuda Exempted Company with non-resident management, a physical meeting with a director or the local Authorised Representative is a de facto regulatory expectation and materially accelerates compliance sign-off. The Bermuda Exempted Company must additionally be registered as an Overseas Company in Gibraltar with a physical registered office and resident director or Authorised Representative under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-exempt status of the Bermuda Exempted Company raising structure-transparency concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda Economic Substance Declaration (Form ES-1) with confirmation of core income generating activities; Bermuda Certificate of Compliance issued by the Bermuda Registrar of Companies; Gibraltar Economic Substance Certificate of Compliance demonstrating the entity meets the UK-style ES test; CRS/FATCA registration certificates evidencing automatic exchange of information enrolment for Gibraltar (GI) and Bermuda (BM); organisational chart showing full chain of ownership from ultimate individual beneficial owners to the operating entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual cross-border retainer flows into the executive search account without contract-linked explanation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed executive search retainer agreements naming the client, search mandate scope, fee schedule and payment terms; itemised invoices per placement milestone; onboarding KYC file on each paying client (corporate registry extract, board resolution authorising the retainer payment); bank statement narrative references aligned to invoice/purpose codes; and for candidate sign-on fee flows, the signed placement agreement and candidate bank account verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate or same-day onward transmission of received funds to third parties (candidate sign-on bonuses or contractor headhunters) triggering layering suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-approved beneficiary file for each candidate or subcontractor containing identity proof, source of funds declaration, signed commission agreement and right-to-work documentation; segregation of client retainer funds in a clearly labelled operational account; board meeting minutes approving the aggregate outbound payment pattern; thresholds triggering a senior compliance review when outbound value exceeds 70% of inbound receipts within 5 business days; legal opinion confirming no restrictions under Gibraltar Sanctions Regulations 2020.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nonexecutive director or shareholder appearing on adverse media or sanction lists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: World-Check or LexisNexis enhanced due diligence reports dated within 90 days; independent legal counsel analysis of media mentions and refutation statements; certified passport and proof of residence documentation for the relevant director or shareholder; confirmation from a licensed Authorised Representative that the Gibraltar beneficial ownership register and the Bermuda beneficial ownership register are current and disclose the control chain completely.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-advantaged territory classification (Gibraltar) paired with opaque US or UK source contracts being flagged for FATCA/CRS mismatch
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FATCA Global Intermediary Identification Number (GIIN) for the Gibraltar entity; CRS self-certification forms for every controlling person, including US origin shareholders with W-8BEN-E; audited financial statements and corporate tax return filing confirmation in Gibraltar; evidence of active management and substance (leased office, resident staff, payroll, board meeting minutes held in Gibraltar) to disprove artificial arrangement treatment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 7830 executive search sector misclassified as high-risk employment agency with cash-heavy operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML risk tier assessment document prepared under GFSC AML/CFT Guidance Notes 2021 classifying the business as Low_Risk_Standard professional services; business plan and fee schedule evidencing contracted retainer billing rather than cash salary disbursement; corporate registration and statutory licence confirmation (Gibraltar Private Employment Agencies licensing under the Private Employment Agencies Regulations if headhunting is conducted within Gibraltar); anti-fraud undertaking and quarterly due diligence refresh commitment letter.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital is injected from the Bermuda Exempted Company's Bermuda domiciliary bank (e.g., Butterfield Bank Bermuda or HSBC Bermuda) via SWIFT MT103 to the Gibraltar International Bank GBP or EUR account. The remittance must include a purpose code mirroring the Bermuda Companies Act share premium contribution and the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 notice of allotment; beneficial owner reference must recite 'Capital Contribution - Allotment of Shares - [Company Name] GI TIN XXX'. The bank will require a board resolution of the Bermuda parent authorising the transfer, a certified copy of the share allotment return filed with the Gibraltar Registrar, and confirmation that no exchange control approval is required by the Gibraltar Currency Commission. For retainer-fee receivables from international clients, the same SWIFT rail is used with purpose code 'Payment for professional services - retainer invoice number' and must be pre-matched to the signed executive search agreement to satisfy source-of-funds validation. Verification protocols include biometric director attestation via the bank's digital onboarding layer and retention of the full SWIFT payment confirmation in the ongoing due diligence file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational trade disbursements run over four clearing rails depending on value, currency, and urgency. (1) SWIFT MT103 is used as the principal rail for international candidate signing bonuses, subcontractor headhunter commissions, and client-rebatable disbursements above GBP 25,000; standard settlement coincides with CHAPS (GBP), SEPA Instant (EUR), and Fedwire (USD) clearing windows. (2) A commercial Letter of Credit (LC) mechanism is established for large contingent-headhunting mandates where the Gibraltar entity acts as an intermediary in employer-to-candidate sign-on fee financing; the LC is confirmed by a first-class UK clearing bank and domiciled in favour of the candidate's bank account, ensuring the search firm never holds unsecured working capital. (3) Faster Payments (in GBP) and SEPA Credit Transfer (in EUR) are used for sub-threshold operational payments such as candidate expense reimbursements, vendor subscription payments, and payroll disbursements enacted via the Gibraltar payroll bank account. (4) Wise B2B API is integrated as a fallback rail for emergency cross-border payments to remote contractors at restrictive banking corridors; all Wise outbound transactions are mapped to the underlying invoice in the treasury management system, and daily exposure via EMI channels is capped at 10% of aggregate monthly outflows. Disbursement rules require dual-approval for any transaction above GBP 5,000, a quarterly review of the sanctioned-beneficiary list, and full electronic reconciliation against the hired-candidate placement records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright GBP/EUR and GBP/USD FX forwards up to 12-month tenors under an ISDA/IFEMA 2005 Master Agreement with the Gibraltar clearing bank, used exclusively to lock the margin on multi-currency retainer contracts
Plain vanilla cross-currency swaps (GBP collateralised, EUR/USD coupon legs) for matching long-duration receivables denominated in EUR or USD against GBP-denominated payroll and rent liabilities

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market currencies (e.g., INR, BRL, NGN, MXN) where local candidate sign-on fees are payable and the underlying currency is non-convertible offshore; NDFs are limited to notional amounts strictly equal to the confirmed foreign-currency liability and settled in GBP
Foreign-exchange spot contracts executed via the bank's dealing desk or electronic FX platform for daily operational conversion within a pre-approved net open position limit of GBP 250,000

Zero-cost collars (put/call combination on EUR/GBP) for retainer pipelines exceeding GBP 1 million, subject to treasury committee approval proving hedge effectiveness and prohibiting speculative trading

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Overseas Company Annual Return for a Bermuda Exempted Company registered as a foreign company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies / Companies House Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return must be delivered at least once in each calendar year, not later than 42 days after the anniversary of the date of Gibraltar registration; if the company is tax-exempt in Bermuda, a nil-return confirmation is still required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a fixed penalty of GBP 100 for the first month and GBP 50 for each subsequent month up to GBP 500; continued default can result in the Registrar striking the foreign company off the Gibraltar overseas-company register and closure of the branch.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Exempted Company Annual Government Fee and Registration Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies / Government of Bermuda Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual fee payable on or before 31 July for the Government fee year running 1 July to 30 June; new exempted companies pay a pro-rated fee at incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers an automatic late-fee penalty of USD 200 or 10% of the unpaid fee, whichever is higher; after three months of outstanding fees the Bermuda Registrar may suspend the company's compliance certificate, restrict transactions, and initiate strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Secure Search (BOSS) Annual Confirmation / UBO Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies via the BOSS portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation must be completed by 31 July each year; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the triggering event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence under Bermuda's Beneficial Ownership (Amendment) Act 2018; fines may reach USD 22,500 plus daily default penalties of USD 300, and repeated failure can lead to company dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Corporate Tax Confirmation and Economic Substance Declaration (if managed and controlled in Gibraltar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Corporate tax return due by 30 November for calendar-year accounting periods, or within 12 months of the financial year-end; economic substance declaration must accompany the annual return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of GBP 300 plus daily default penalty up to GBP 60 per day, capped at GBP 10,000; persistent non-filing may result in estimated assessments, public strike-off, and disqualification orders.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Gibraltar branch: statutory audit is required if the foreign company exceeds any two of: annual turnover GBP 6.5 million, balance-sheet total GBP 3.26 million, or average employees 50, in two consecutive years. Bermuda exempted company: audit is compulsory for exempted companies listed on an approved stock exchange, licensed under insurance or investment business legislation, or having gross assets above USD 1.5 million unless a Section 87B audit exemption is granted; a typical executive-search headhunting agency will remain below these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Bermuda statutory accounts must be prepared in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB; Bermuda also permits US GAAP for exempted companies where shareholders so resolve. For Gibraltar branch reporting, IFRS as adopted by the UK/EU applies, and a small qualifying Gibraltar-resident subsidiary may apply FRS 101 only when a parent guarantee is provided.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For a Bermuda Exempted Company, beneficial ownership information must be filed on the BOSS portal within 30 days of any share transfer or change in ownership control, and an annual accuracy confirmation must be completed by the 31 July renewal date. Any share transfer that changes direct or indirect ownership by more than 10% of the issued share capital must be recorded in the Bermuda Register of Members and uploaded to BOSS before the transfer is finalised; if the company maintains a Gibraltar overseas-company register, the Gibraltar branch UBO register must be updated within 14 days of the same event.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 12,000 per annum for a small executive-search agency; USD 15,000 - USD 25,000 if a dual Bermuda and Gibraltar consolidated audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0.00% (Gibraltar standard corporate rate for non-regulated activity; Bermuda imposes no corporate income tax on an Exempted Company)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory 0% headline rate; Bermuda Ministerial Exemption (tax assurance certificate) shields the Exempted Company from any future Bermuda income tax until 31 March 2035; Gibraltar applies a 12.5% rate only to utility and gaming concession enterprises, not to executive search; full exemption from Gibraltar VAT, capital gains tax, inheritance tax, and stamp duty on share transfers; no withholding tax on dividends, interest, or royalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Company Tax Return (Form 3CT) filed electronically through the GOSS (Gibraltar Online Self-Service) portal of the Income Tax Office, H.M. Customs & Income Tax Department; the Companies House Gibraltar registration number must be quoted on the form.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months after the end of the accounting period; a company with a 31 December fiscal year-end must file no later than 31 December of the following year (preceding-year basis of assessment).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal name, Companies House Gibraltar registration number, registered office in Gibraltar, and contact particulars.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Bermuda Exempted Company must state its Bermuda registration number separately from its Gibraltar registration and appoint a Gibraltar resident service address for service of process.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Year of assessment and accounting period covered (opening and closing dates of the basis period).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the actual financial year-end adopted in the Bermuda exempted company accounts; alignment avoids dual basis-period adjustments between Bermuda and Gibraltar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross business receipts from executive search, headhunting retainers, success fees, and candidate placement commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognise revenue per the Bermuda GAAP books; disclose any related-party receipts from UK-linked clients routed through the Gibraltar operating office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: staff costs, search database subscriptions, global professional indemnity insurance, marketing, rent, and legal fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany management charges from the Bermuda parent must be supported by written agreements and priced at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital allowances claimed on fixed assets: office equipment, leasehold improvements, and software licences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned assets deployed in Gibraltar qualify for allowances; assets used solely in Bermuda are excluded from the Gibraltar computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net chargeable income or adjusted taxable profits (Box 3 minus Box 4 minus Box 5).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where central management and control (CMC) is contended to sit in Bermuda, enter £nil and attach a residency analysis with board-meeting records and decision-making evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at the applicable rate: 0% for non-regulated executive search activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm zero tax liability even where profits arise, as the 0% standard rate applies to all non-utility activities in Gibraltar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses carried forward and set-off claimed (restricted to five years under the adopted compliance rule).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a continuity-of-trade schedule proving the executive headhunting trade remained identical during the loss year and that the loss was not generated through contrived related-party invoicing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: immediate fixed penalty of GBP 100 plus a daily penalty of GBP 10 (capped at GBP 1,000), followed by a Commissioner's best-of-judgment assessment; inaccurate returns carry penalties of up to 100% of the tax understated with interest at the statutory rate; late Companies House Gibraltar annual return incurs GBP 200 for the first month and GBP 100 for each additional month.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Bermuda Annual Company Return filed with the Registrar of Companies via the Bermuda Registry e-Filing portal, accompanied by the Annual Compliance and Economic Substance Declaration (ESD) where a relevant activity exists; the annual government fee secures corporate existence for the following year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual government fee and Annual Return due by 31 January of each year in respect of the preceding calendar year; the ESR/ESD declaration must be filed within six months of the financial year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identity: Bermuda company number, exempted status affirmation, and registered office address in Bermuda.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A registered-agent office in Bermuda satisfies the physical presence requirement; the exempted company may be 100% foreign owned, and non-resident ownership is permissible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity: C-Suite Executive Search and Specialist Tech Headhunting (ISIC 7830 / NAICS 561312).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the Gibraltar-based operations; the Bermuda entity must not purport to conduct local trading activity inside Bermuda.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorised and issued share capital schedule used to compute the annual government fee.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The fee is calculated on the maximum permitted capital authorised; presenting an excessive authorised capital without issued shares will not reduce the fee liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Register of directors, officers, shareholders, and beneficial owners required under the Companies and Limited Liability Companies Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the beneficial ownership register mandated by the Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Act; non-resident directors are permitted and no local residence qualification applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Economic substance declaration: headcount, premises, and core income-generating activities (CIGA) located in Gibraltar.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that outsourcing arrangements do not strip substance; CIGA must be managed and performed in the operating jurisdiction (Gibraltar), not in the Bermuda head office.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late government fee: monthly surcharge of 0.9% of the unpaid fee; late Annual Return: administrative penalty at the Registrar's discretion of up to USD 25,000 plus daily default penalties; persistent non-filing results in strike-off of exempted status and loss of the ministerial tax-assurance shield.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0.00% — Gibraltar imposes no withholding tax on dividends paid to a Bermuda Exempted Company shareholder or to any non-resident; Bermuda levies no dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because the statutory rate is 0%, no conventional DTA reduction is ordinarily required; where a relief claim is nonetheless necessary (e.g., to refresh a beneficial-ownership certificate or where a UK payer asserts the UK–Gibraltar DTA), the protocol is: (i) obtain a Gibraltar Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the Income Tax Office based on CMC and VAT registration; (ii) file the standard WHT relief form with the Gibraltar paying agent or UK payer before the payment date; (iii) attach the Bermuda tax-exemption certificate evidencing beneficial ownership; (iv) if tax is deducted at source, apply for a refund within five years under the Income Tax Act.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Gibraltar statutory withholding tax on royalties paid for IP (search databases, software licences) is 0%, and interest paid to non-residents is 0%; under the UK–Gibraltar DTA, UK-origin interest remains taxable only in Gibraltar at 0%, and royalties are exempt from UK source-state withholding in most classifications; Bermuda imposes no withholding tax on royalties or interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory contemporaneous Local File where gross revenue exceeds GBP 8,000,000 or where cross-border related-party transactions exceed GBP 500,000; a Master File is required where consolidated group revenue exceeds GBP 50,000,000; executive search retainers paid by UK parent-linked clients are within scope even below the revenue threshold where intercompany value exceeds GBP 500,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Gibraltar's Economic Substance (Company) Regulations 2019 and Bermuda's Economic Substance Regulations 2019 apply concurrently. Executive search is classified as a service business / headquarters relevant activity for ESR purposes. The company must annually demonstrate: (i) locally managed board meetings and strategy sessions in Gibraltar; (ii) a physical office and an adequate, proportionate workforce in Gibraltar; (iii) CIGA performed in Gibraltar (client sourcing, candidate identification, retainer negotiation, delivery of placement, invoicing); (iv) no outsourcing of CIGA to the Bermuda parent without documented commercial rationale; and (v) filing of the ESR declaration within six months of the financial year-end.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally filing a false nil return, omitting success fees received from UK client campaigns, or fabricating deductible placement fees to create artificial losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of up to 100% of the tax understated plus daily default surcharges and interest at the statutory rate; criminal conviction on indictment carries an unlimited fine and imprisonment for up to seven years; forfeiture of the proceeds of the offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors who directed or consented to the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the company's restitution; courts may issue worldwide asset freezing orders, travel bans, and disqualification orders of up to 15 years; convicted directors face imprisonment for up to seven years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Bermuda Exempted Company as a paper entity with no Gibraltar office, no local employees, contracts negotiated remotely from Bermuda or the UK, and all core income-generating activities performed outside Gibraltar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR penalty of up to GBP 100,000 plus additional daily penalties of up to GBP 10,000 per day of non-compliance; compulsory strike-off from the Gibraltar Companies Registry; automatic exchange of information with HMRC, Bermuda, and the OECD framework; termination of Bermuda exempted status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for unpaid ESR penalties where the directors caused the non-compliance; disqualification from acting as a director for up to 10 years; liability for restoration costs following strike-off; exposure to fraud-based preference claims in an insolvent liquidation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering, Sanctions, and Statutory Licensing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting executive search retainers from shell-company clients linked to PEPs or sanctions-listed persons, failing KYC/EDD, processing fees through opaque third-country conduits or cryptocurrencies, or operating without the statutory headhunting licence required under Gibraltar employment and recruitment agencies legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlimited fine on conviction under the Gibraltar Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 and sanctions regulations; additional regulator fines of up to GBP 1,000,000; revocation of the statutory licence; compliance notices and business suspension; restraint and confiscation orders against the firm.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability for failure to file suspicious-activity reports, with imprisonment of up to 14 years for money laundering; civil liability for regulatory fines where the board failed to install a compliant AML framework; travel restrictions and property restraints; disqualification from serving as a director for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Double Taxation Arrangement Abuse and Synthetic Routing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring UK-origin headhunting fees to flow through a Gibraltar shelf entity into a Bermuda entity solely to invoke UK–Gibraltar DTA relief or the 0% Gibraltar regime while central management and control remains in the UK.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and reassessment at UK taxpayer level with penalties up to 100%; disallowance of Gibraltar nil-rate claims; exchange of information with HMRC under the DTA/TIEA network; OECD principal-purpose-test countermeasures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve synthetic routing face personal restitution orders and potential liability under the UK Criminal Finances Act 2017 failure-to-prevent-facilitation-of-tax-evasion offence, carrying imprisonment up to seven years; civil recovery of double benefit plus interest; HMRC director-level penalty notices; travel bans pending cross-border investigation.
